name: ʿAnbasa ibn Maʿdān al-Mahrī, known as ʿAnbasa al-Fīl
summary: Basran pupil of Abū al-Aswad, named 'the Elephant' after his father's keeping of a governor's elephant; by Abū ʿUbayda's account the ablest of Abū al-Aswad's pupils.
bio: ʿAnbasa was the son of Maʿdān, a man of Maysān who settled in Basra and was called 'Maʿdān of the Elephant' because he took over the upkeep of the elephant of the governor ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir. ʿAnbasa learned grammar from Abū al-Aswad al-Duʾalī and transmitted poetry, among it Jarīr's, for which al-Farazdaq lampooned him and his father's elephant.

Ibn al-Anbārī reports from Abū ʿUbayda that of those who came to Abū al-Aswad to learn Arabic, ʿAnbasa was the ablest, and that Maymūn al-Aqran then studied with him; al-Zubaydī places him in the second generation of the grammarians of Basra. The year of his death is not recorded.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 15–17
